text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to close at $131.83, continuing a sharp two-week decline that accelerated sharply on September 16th when the stock dropped over $8 in a single day. While crude oil prices remain elevated globally (Brent at $130.80/barrel), the broader energy sector appears to be pricing in recession risk from sustained high fuel costs—record diesel prices are already hammering transportation, a sign that prolonged energy inflation could slow economic growth and reduce overall fuel demand.

The Middle East escalation (Iran closing the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks, incidents near Saudi airports) created supply-shock headlines that initially pushed oil higher, but markets seem to have concluded the disruption is manageable or that any short-term supply tightness will be offset by weaker economic demand if energy costs remain this high. The stock's decline from $141 down to $131 over three trading days suggests investors are weighing the demand destruction from high prices more heavily than the supply-disruption upside.
